messages.subject: Predictions in hierarchical model
parts:
Hello everyone,
i have a situation where I want to generate predicted values from a binomial hierarchical model. I've got a model such as:

fit<- inla(y ~ x + f(group, model ="iid"), family="binomial", data=mydata, Ntrials=1)

I know from the FAQ that if I want to get fitted values from the model, I can basically include new values of 'x' in my data, with y == NA, and I will get fitted values for those cases. My question is, what about the hierarchical level? I.e. what if I have a new level of 'group' that isn't originally observed, but I want to use the posterior predictive distribution to estimate the value for a new group?

Any advice would be welcome.
-Corey

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Predictions in hierarchical model
parts:
On Mon, 2017-04-17 at 10:48 -0700, Corey Sparks wrote:
>
> fit<- inla(y ~ x + f(group, model ="iid"), family="binomial",
> data=mydata, Ntrials=1)
>
> I know from the FAQ that if I want to get fitted values from the
> model, I can basically include new values of 'x' in my data, with y
> == NA, and I will get fitted values for those cases. My question is,
> what about the hierarchical level? I.e. what if I have a new level of
> 'group' that isn't originally observed, but I want to use the
> posterior predictive distribution to estimate the value for a new
> group?

you can set

y[i] = NA
group[i] = 13

assuming 13 a new a new level. then 'group[i]' will be predicted from
its posterior and you'll get that effect into the linear predictor and
fitted values.
